correctness.rationale: Restricting the product code to inputs u_i c turns every computation slot into a_i c for a=uGcomp. Expanding the coordinates a_i in a B-basis of their span expresses every identical product leakage g_j(a_i c_j) as a B-linear combination of at most rho_B(a) base leakages g_j(alpha_l c_j). Product reconstruction then recovers a nonzero scalar multiple of the base secret. For a systematic single-output code, rank one is exactly dependence of the coefficient classes in F/B; independence excludes rank one while each generator row has rank two. The finite-field verifier matches these identities exhaustively in representative small extensions.

originality.rationale: The motivating Aoutouf--Augot paper was checked in its LERS, general computation-code, rank-criterion, numerical-example, and identical-leakage sections. It proves collapse for simple addition and reports simulations for weighted sums and LFSRs, but does not state the minimum-subfield-rank transfer theorem, the projective subfield-word obstruction, or the quotient-space classification. Searches using equivalent leakage, repair, subfield-rank, projective-subfield, and quotient-space terminology found no matching theorem, and the SCOPE archive has no overlapping secret-sharing/LERS record. Priority risk remains elevated because the motivating preprint is recent.

value.rationale: A single computation-code invariant now explains both the impossibility for ordinary addition and the accumulation possible in LFSRs. The one-output specialization is sharp: the minimum rank is exactly one or two, gives the barrier K >= [F:B], and shows that every two-input weighted relation over a quadratic extension collapses to a base one-subsymbol repair regardless of coefficient distinctness.
